original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[x1, ..., xn] with n > 1, and let Aut*_k(k[x1, ..., xn]) be the subgroup of polynomial automorphisms whose Jacobian determinant is 1. Let T = {diag(t1, ..., tn) | product_{i=1}^n ti = 1} be the diagonal torus acting by xi -> ti xi. A nonzero locally nilpotent derivation D of k[x1, ..., xn] is called a root vector with respect to T if there exists a nontrivial character chi: T -> G_m such that sigma o D o sigma^{-1} = chi(sigma) D for every sigma in T. Which characters chi occur as roots of Aut*_k(k[x1, ..., xn]) with respect to T, and which locally nilpotent derivations D are the corresponding root vectors?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.1, immediately following Definition 1.1: find all roots and root vectors of Aut_k^* k[n] with respect to the diagonal torus T. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the formal content of the paper's target problem: the base field is algebraically closed of characteristic 0, the ambient algebra is k[x_1,...,x_n] with n > 1, the group is the Jacobian-1 subgroup Aut_k^* k[n], the torus T is the diagonal torus with product t_i = 1, the notion of root vector is restricted to nonzero locally nilpotent derivations, and the question asks for the complete classification of roots and corresponding root vectors.
missing_details: State explicitly that D is a k-derivation of k[x_1,...,x_n], matching Definition 1.1.
Define 'locally nilpotent' in stand-alone form: for every f in k[x_1,...,x_n], there exists m = m(f) >= 1 such that D^m(f) = 0.
Specify that G_m is the multiplicative group over k and that chi is a nontrivial character in Hom(T, G_m).
Make explicit that the problem is only about roots and root vectors with respect to this fixed torus T; the neighboring Problem 1.2 on the centralizer and normalizer of T is a different question.

For full paper-faithfulness, include the surrounding Section 1 context that T is singled out because n - 1 is the maximal possible dimension of an algebraic torus in Aut_k^* k[n], and every such torus is conjugate to T.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[n] := k[x_1,...,x_n] with n > 1, and let Aut_k^* k[n] := {sigma in Aut_k k[n] | det((partial sigma(x_j)/partial x_i)_(1<=i,j<=n)) = 1}. Let T := {diag(t_1,...,t_n) in Aut_k^* k[n] | sigma(x_i) = t_i x_i, t_i in k, and product_{i=1}^n t_i = 1}. A nonzero locally nilpotent k-derivation D of k[n] (that is, for every f in k[n] there exists m = m(f) >= 1 with D^m(f) = 0) is called a root vector of Aut_k^* k[n] with respect to T if there exists a nontrivial character chi: T -> G_m such that sigma o D o sigma^{-1} = chi(sigma)D for every sigma in T; chi is then called the corresponding root. Find all roots and all root vectors of Aut_k^* k[n] with respect to T.
justification: The draft clearly targets the first problem in Section 1: Definition 1.1 gives exactly the root/root-vector notion for Aut_k^* k[n] relative to T, and Problem 1.1 then asks to find all such roots and root vectors. The paragraph immediately before Definition 1.1 supplies the hidden scope of the torus T by explaining its maximality and conjugacy among (n-1)-dimensional tori in Aut_k^* k[n]. I therefore kept the question fixed to that torus and did not broaden it to the separate centralizer/normalizer question of Problem 1.2. No explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 1.1 is stated in the paper, so equivalent_formulation is null. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
